name: Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument
author: parks-page-legacy
summary: Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument in southwestern Arizona protects 330,689 acres of Sonoran Desert wilderness along the U.S.–Mexico border — the only place in the United States where the organ pipe cactus grows wild. Proclaimed a national monument in 1937, the park was designated a UNESCO International Biosphere Reserve in 1976 in recognition of its outstanding desert ecosystem biodiversity. The monument harbors 28 species of cactus, over 270 species of birds, and rare mammals including the Sonoran pronghorn, one of the most endangered land mammals in North America. The Tohono O'odham people have lived in and around the monument's lands for centuries and maintain cultural connections to the landscape. The monument's location on the international border has made it a focal point in immigration and border security debates.
